content:
We are pleased to announce the Lean Together 2026 conference!
Similarly to previous years, it will be an online event, 19-23 January 2026, so mark those dates on your calendars. We'll schedule things starting at different times on different days, to account for various timezones.

We'll reach out to some of you directly about giving talks, but we'd also like to solicit contributed talks from the community. Anything Lean, or formalization-related, is in scope. A big point of these workshops is to get an idea of what other people around the world are working on and to coordinate efforts. We're not only looking for polished conference talks, and we'd like to leave plenty of time for discussion. Students, faculty, professional programmers, industry partners: all are welcome.

We will attempt to develop a balanced, interesting, and diverse program that offers options across the spectrum of Lean usage. If you are interested in giving a talk, you may submit an abstract by 1 December 2025.
The number of slots being finite, we will very likely be forced to make some choices and unfortunately not everybody interested will have the opportunity to speak, but please don't be shy and propose a talk!

The organizers of Lean Together 2026,
Rémy Degenne , Markus Himmel , Jireh Loreaux , Patrick Massot

Reminder: if you are interested in giving a talk at Lean Together 2026, please submit an abstract by 1 December 2025.
(I won't spam this channel with further reminders)

The Lean Together 2026 conference starts tomorrow! We will begin at 2026-01-19T15:00:00+01:00 with a few opening remarks, and then for the first talk of the conference, Johan Commelin will present the new Mathlib Initiative.
Check out the full schedule at https://leanprover-community.github.io/lt2026/schedule.html
For discussion of the talks, and any other topic related to the conference, go to the #Lean Together 2026 channel.
